image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of the head and upper jaw of a Nile crocodile. The image focuses on the textured, armored skin (scutes), the eye with a vertical pupil, and the interlocking teeth along the jawline. The background is a blurred, out-of-focus green/brown, suggesting a natural habitat.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is broad and triangular with a V-shaped snout (narrower than alligator).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible portion of the snout tapers to a point, consistent with the V-shape of a crocodile rather than the U-shape of an alligator. The head structure appears robust.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Jaws are massive with numerous conical, interlocking teeth visible when mouth is closed.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Multiple conical teeth are clearly visible. The fourth lower tooth appears to fit into a notch or sit alongside the upper jaw, consistent with crocodilian anatomy. Teeth look sharp and distinct, not melted.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Eyes are positioned dorsally on the head with vertical slit pupils and a nictitating membrane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The eye is positioned high on the skull. The pupil is a distinct vertical slit. The surrounding eyelid structure is complex but anatomically plausible for a reptile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Nostrils are positioned at the tip of the snout.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tip of the snout is cut off by the right edge of the frame; nostrils are not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is elongated and heavily armored.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible neck and shoulder region show heavy, thick armor plating consistent with an elongated body structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is covered in thick, bony scutes (osteoderms) arranged in regular longitudinal rows along the dorsal surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin texture is highly detailed, showing irregular but structured bony plates (scutes) with deep crevices, matching the description of osteoderms.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Scutes are dark brown to grey with a rough, heavily textured appearance.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The coloration is a mix of greys and browns. The texture is visibly rough and granular, not smooth or plastic-like.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Ventral surface is covered in smooth, rectangular scales that are pale yellow to white.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside (belly) of the crocodile is not visible in this profile shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Limbs are short and stout with webbed feet; forelimbs have five digits, hind limbs have four.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: No limbs or feet are visible in the cropped headshot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is laterally compressed and muscular, comprising half of total body length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is outside the frame.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species (Nile Crocodile vs. other crocodilians) based on snout shape and scale pattern.
To detect subtle AI artifacts in the complex geometry of the teeth and the high-frequency noise of the skin scales.
To ensure the boundary between the teeth/gums and the background is sharp and that the eye structure is topologically sound (no melting into the socket).

focus_areas: Integrity of individual teeth (no fusion or extra teeth)
Realism of skin pore/scute texture (no repetitive patterns or smearing)
Anatomical correctness of the eye and eyelid structure
Edge sharpness against the blurred background
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the teeth. AI often struggles with the precise interlocking mechanism of crocodile jaws. Check if any teeth appear to float, merge with the gum line, or have inconsistent lighting. Also, verify the eye's reflection and pupil shape for biological plausibility.
